text:
maria: FYI — after merging the pos-enc kernel refactor (ROPE -> unified posenc path) we saw a small but consistent drift in long-seq attention scores when ALiBi is enabled. repro on T4 and A100 in nightly. putting notes here for follow-up.

jake: :eyes: how small? relative to FP32 baseline?

maria: ~1e-3 difference in attention logits at seq 4096, grows with length. outputs diverge after ~1k tokens for some prompts. FP32 baseline matches master; new kernel uses fp16 path with fp32 accumulation.

sam: can you paste a minimal repro and failing diff?

maria: logs: 
```
# short excerpt
seq=4096 model=redwood/llama-13b
old_kernel max_logit=12.34567
new_kernel max_logit=12.34421
diff=0.00146
```
Also saw NaN once when running with aggressive quantization flags.

lee: NaN sounds like overflow in the positional scale or range reduction bug. ALiBi multiplies slopes by position idx; if idx scaled into fp16 that can under/overflow.

frances: did we change the exponent / trig evaluation for ROPE? I remember we switched to a fused sincos approx optimized for Ampere.

maria: yes — we switched to a fast sincos poly approx and to `__half` storage for the precomputed cos/sin table. accumulation into fp32 during dot. That seemed safe but repro shows tiny bias.

jake: tradeoff: speed vs reproducibility. For production we need deterministic behavior across GPUs if possible, or at least tests that detect regressions. cost of reverting to full fp32 table might be high.

sam: quick analysis: two plausible sources: (1) polynomial sincos error introduces phase error -> rotated q/k mismatch, (2) ALiBi slope multiplication in fp16 loses low-order bits for large pos -> subtle bias. Can you try: keep sincos poly but precompute tables in fp32 and cast, or keep fp16 table but use range reduction to small angles before poly?

maria: tried precompute in fp32 then cast to fp16 at use-time — still sees diff but smaller (~5e-4). keeping fp32 tables (no cast) removes drift entirely in my runs.

lee: that suggests table quantization is the main culprit. Using fp16 storage reduced memory but introduced quantization of sin/cos. For ROPE, small phase errors amplify after many rotations because each attention step multiplies through.

frances: performance hit measured?

maria: full fp32 table -> kernel latency +6% on A100, +10% on T4 in microbench. Impact on end-to-end generation latency smaller due to batching.

jake: options: (A) revert to fp32 tables for correctness and add a config knob to enable fp16 low-memory mode; (B) keep fp16 but add compensated multiplication (Kahan-style) or use mixed-precision tricks; (C) improve sincos approx error via higher-order poly and range reduction.

sam: also consider ALiBi slopes: we can store slopes in fp32 even if cos/sin in fp16. That reduces slope quantization problem.

maria: NaN case seems separate: when quant+fused kernels + very long pos -> occasionally angle reduction produced NaN in poly due to bad branch. I have a failing trace and a small fix to guard.

ci-bot: deploy/built #3791 succeeded on canary.

lee: proposal from eng-runtime: patch1: revert to fp32 precomputed tables by default; add a runtime flag `POSENC_FP16_TABLE=1` to opt-in to fp16; patch2: add unit tests covering seq lengths [512,1024,2048,4096] comparing to fp32 reference with target tol=1e-4; patch3: guard NaN path in fused sincos poly.

frances: sounds reasonable. Need perf regression PR with microbench numbers and optionality documented in the runtime config. Also add a note in the Optimize guide about memory/perf tradeoff.

jake: agree. Also add a canary rollout plan: route 5% of traffic on hosted to new kernel with fp32 tables, 0% to fp16 opt until we verify. If errors or increased 99th tail latency >10% rollback.

sam: one more thing — for ALiBi we could normalize position indexes by chunk size and store scaled slopes to reduce dynamic range. That might allow fp16 safely. Worth a follow-up RFC but not needed for immediate fix.

maria: I'll open PRs: one bugfix (NaN guard), one revert-to-fp32-tables with flag + tests, and one perf doc. Expected timeline: bugfix today, fp32 revert + tests by EOD tomorrow.

lee: thanks. can someone pair-review the perf PR? @frances?

frances: I can review. also will run extended nightly on A100 and T4.

jake: thanks team. add the perf numbers to the rollback checklist.

maria: will do. tagging this thread in the RFC follow-up card. :white_check_mark:

sam: small follow-up: let's add a reproducible fuzz harness that randomizes seq lengths and uses fp64 reference to catch subtle bit-level regressions early.

maria: yep adding that to tests.

frances: merging plan: bugfix -> canary -> perf PR -> full rollout.

maria: updated: pushed NaN guard (PR #4012), test CI passed. I'll open the fp32-table PR next.

ci-bot: PR #4012 merged by maria (main).
